Frontend: landing page renders unauthenticated with all required testids (nav-signup-btn, nav-login-btn, hero-signup-btn, cta-signup-btn, landing-plan-monthly/quarterly/annual) and all four programmes (Yoga, Strength & Conditioning, Muscle Building, Fat Loss); every signup/login button routes to /login. Admin login lands on /admin with 4 stat cards, sidebar visible, admin-users-list showing all 13 seeded users, 13 role-select-* dropdowns; clicking manage-sub-{id} opens membership-modal with grant-monthly/quarterly/annual and revoke-membership buttons; granting monthly persists (toast 'Granted Monthly to Temp User.' + Monthly chip + active_members stat increments 0→1). Trainer login (sarah.trainer) lands on /trainer with trainer-specialty input, day-0..6 toggles (Mon–Fri highlighted), time-06:00..20:00 toggles (07/08/09/17/18/19 highlighted), save-availability-btn, and trainer-sessions-list showing the client-created booking with a Join button. Client login (pwuser) lands on /dashboard; /booking shows 4 trainer cards, booking-date picker, slot-<time> buttons after picking a Monday, confirm-booking-btn creates a booking that appears in bookings-list with Unpaid chip and join-{id}. Clicking Join navigates to /call/{bookingId}, which renders the header 'Session with Sarah Johnson · date · time · specialty', leave-call-btn, and mounts jitsi-container; the Jitsi external_api.js loads meet.jit.si and shows the 'Join meeting' prejoin page (call was not actually completed, per instructions). Cancel booking works.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 960 lines — was 762 in iteration_3. Getting close to the 700-line soft cap being materially exceeded. Recommend splitting into routers: /routers/auth.py, /routers/trainers_bookings.py, /routers/admin.py, /routers/payments.py, /routers/ai.py — the module boundaries are already clean in the current sectioned layout so extraction is low-risk.

seed_roles() runs on every backend startup but only inserts if the user is missing — good, idempotent. However when a client is promoted to trainer via /admin/users/{id}/role, only default_days/times/specialty are seeded if the target has NO available_times yet — a subsequent admin demoting them back to client leaves the trainer fields lingering on the doc (they become invisible but cost storage). Consider clearing specialty/available_* on demotion, or filter them out of admin_users response for non-trainers.

GET /api/sessions/{booking_id} allows either the booking's user_id OR trainer_id — correct scoping. Room name derives from booking id (deterministic), so both parties join the same Jitsi room without needing a shared secret exchange. Good design.

VideoCall.js loads https://meet.jit.si/external_api.js on demand and disposes the API on unmount — clean; the ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME messages seen in console come from Jitsi's mobile-app deep links (jitsi-meet://, tel:), harmless in a browser test.

AdminPanel role dropdown uses a plain HTML <select>. It works and is accessible, but the clay/glass design language uses custom pills elsewhere — a shadcn Select would look more consistent. Non-blocking.

Trainer promotion via /admin/users/{id}/role seeds available_days=DEFAULT_DAYS but stores the LIVE list reference (DEFAULT_DAYS is a module-level list). If anything later mutates DEFAULT_DAYS in memory, every promoted trainer's row is affected. Mongo insert immediately serialises so this is currently safe, but defensive copy (list(DEFAULT_DAYS)) is trivially safer.
